head.intro: Who approves purchase orders before they are sent, how far a delivery may differ from the order, and how suppliers are asked to confirm.

live.changedBody: Your changes on this page are kept until you read again; saving now may be refused because the settings moved on.

scope.label: Whose settings
scope.companyHint: The settings of {company}. Where it keeps none of its own, it follows every company’s.
scope.allHint: The settings every company follows where it keeps none of its own.

noAccess.title: Purchasing settings are not in your role
noAccess.body: Reading them needs the right to see purchasing (purchasing.view). An administrator gives it in Admin › Roles & permissions.

approval.title: PO approval
approval.description: Who approves which purchase orders before they are sent. The rules are written and switched in Admin › Approvals, automation & AI › Approval rules.
approval.locked: Nobody approves their own request, the Owner included.

state.NONE: No approval rule for purchase orders: every order is sent without anyone’s yes.
state.OFF_one: {count} rule written, switched off: every order is sent without anyone’s yes until a rule is switched on.
state.OFF_other: {count} rules written, none switched on: every order is sent without anyone’s yes until a rule is switched on.
state.ON_one: {count} rule of {total} switched on: an order it holds waits for a yes before it is sent.
state.ON_other: {count} rules of {total} switched on: an order they hold waits for a yes before it is sent.

approval.notYetInForce_one: {count} more is switched on from a later date.
approval.notYetInForce_other: {count} more are switched on from a later date.

empty.title: No purchase order rule yet
empty.body: Without a rule every purchase order is sent without a yes. A new rule is written switched off; it asks only once you switch it on.

approval.firstDecides: Several rules may hold for one order: the first one whose approver is not the person asking decides.
approval.comesLater: Comes later: approving from a link in the e-mail, and two approvers one after the other.
approval.inbox: The orders waiting for a yes are in

tolerance.title: Delivery tolerances
tolerance.description: How far a delivery may be over or under the ordered quantity, per supplier or material (for example ±5 % on leather footage).
tolerance.defaultHint: Every supplier and every material. A rule per supplier or material below wins over it.
tolerance.overHint: How much more than ordered is taken, in percent. For example 5.
tolerance.underHint: How much less still counts as delivered in full, in percent. For example 5.

beyondHint.BLOCK: The receipt takes at most the limit; the rest goes back to the supplier.
beyondHint.APPROVAL: The receipt waits for a yes from the buyer before it is posted (recorded in the office; the goods-in tablet refuses the extra).

tolerance.none: No tolerance: a delivery is taken exactly as ordered; more only with the receiver’s reason.
tolerance.table: Delivery tolerances per supplier or material

empty.title: No rule per supplier or material
empty.body: Every delivery follows the default above. Add a rule where one supplier or one material needs its own.

emptyArchived.title: No archived rule
emptyArchived.body: An archived rule no longer applies; it can be reactivated here.

tolerance.precedence: The most specific rule wins: a material over its kind over every material, then a supplier over every supplier, then the company over every company.
tolerance.leatherLine: A leather line that carries its own area tolerance, agreed on its order, keeps it: over it the receiver says why the extra is taken.
tolerance.short: A short delivery is never refused: within the tolerance under, the line counts as received in full.

row.archiveHint: It stops applying; it can be reactivated.

dialog.whoseHint: Every company’s rule is kept only by a role over every company.
dialog.supplierHint: One supplier or workshop, or every supplier.
dialog.materialHint: One material, one kind of material, or every material. A rule names a supplier, a material or both.
dialog.noteHint: Optional: what was agreed and with whom.
dialog.scopeFixed: Whose, supplier and material never change: archive this rule and add another.
dialog.archived: Archived: it no longer applies. Reactivate it to use it again.

confirm.title: Confirmation
confirm.description: When suppliers are asked to confirm an order, and how they are reminded.
confirm.byValue: {hours} hours after the send: {days} of the supplier’s open days, longer over its closed days.
confirm.byHint: The buyer may ask for another time when sending, and move it while the order waits. A setting of its own for this default comes later.
confirm.how: When on, the daily run mails a supplier who has not confirmed by the deadline, then once a day, at most {most} times per revision.
confirm.byHand: A reminder sent by hand from the order counts too. When off, the buyer reminds by hand.
confirm.mails: The reminder repeats the order’s number and its confirm-by time and attaches the order again; it carries no link (a reply from the supplier gets a new one).
confirm.turningOn: Switching on mails real suppliers every day an order waits past its confirm-by time. Saving asks you to confirm it’s you.

on.TENANT: On: it follows every company’s setting.

off.COMPANY: Off for this company: the daily run sends no reminder.
off.TENANT: Off: it follows every company’s setting; the daily run sends no reminder.
off.DEFAULT: Off (never switched on): the daily run sends no reminder.

alert.title: Buyer alert
alert.hint: The buyer is told when an order is still not confirmed after its confirm-by time (Home › Alerts).
alert.none: No alert rule for orders not confirmed: the buyer is not told.

held.offline: Offline: changes are kept on this page until the connection is back.
held.offlineBody: This is the last copy read. Nothing can be saved until the connection is back.
held.noApprovalsView: Reading the approval rules needs the right to see approvals (approvals.view).
held.noRulesManage: Writing approval rules needs the right to keep them (approvals.rules.manage): the Owner or an administrator.
held.noToleranceRight: Keeping delivery tolerances needs purchasing.tolerances.manage over this company.
held.noToleranceRightAll: Every company’s tolerances are kept only by a role over every company.
held.noSwitch: Only the Owner switches automatic reminders to suppliers on or off.
held.noSwitchAll: The reminders of every company are switched only by a role over every company.
held.noAlertsView: Reading alert rules needs the right to see alerts (alerts.view).
held.noPartiesView: Choosing a supplier needs the right to see suppliers (parties.view): the rule is for every supplier.
held.noMaterialsView: Choosing one material needs the right to see materials (product.materials.view): choose a kind instead.
held.noneActive: None of the ticked rules is active, or you may not change them.
held.noneArchived: None of the ticked rules is archived, or you may not change them.

problem.supplierRefused: This supplier cannot take a tolerance: choose another, or every supplier.
problem.exceptionNeedsScope: Name a supplier, a material or both: the default above is for every supplier and every material.
problem.sameScope: An active rule for the same supplier and material exists already: change that one, or archive it first.
problem.toleranceGone: That tolerance is not there any more.

read.signed_out: Your session ended: sign in again.
read.forbidden: Your role does not read this.
read.not_found: Not found: it may have been removed.
read.unavailable: The factory server did not answer. Try again in a moment.
read.rate_limited: Too many tries at once. Wait a moment and try again.
read.contract: This screen and the server do not agree on the answer. Reload the page.
read.internal: Something went wrong reading this. Try again.

write.moved: Someone changed it meanwhile: it is read again and nothing was overwritten. Make your change again.
write.sameScope: An active rule for the same supplier and material exists already: change that one, or archive it first.
write.state: It changed state meanwhile: it is read again.
write.invalid: The server refused what was typed: see the fields.
write.forbidden: Your role may not change this for this company.
write.forbiddenAll: Every company’s settings are changed only by a role over every company.
write.not_found: Not found: it may have been removed. It is read again.
write.signed_out: Your session ended: sign in again, then save.
write.rate_limited: Too many tries at once. Wait a moment and save again.
write.unavailable: The factory server did not answer: nothing was saved. Try again.
write.internal: Something went wrong: nothing was saved. Try again.

done.defaultRemoved: The default is archived: deliveries follow what is in force above it. It can be reactivated from the archived rules.
done.archivedSome_one: {count} of {total} rules archived; the others were refused (read again).
done.archivedSome_other: {count} of {total} rules archived; the others were refused (read again).
done.reactivatedSome_one: {count} of {total} rules reactivated; the others were refused (read again).
done.reactivatedSome_other: {count} of {total} rules reactivated; the others were refused (read again).
done.remindersOn: Automatic reminders are on: the daily run reminds suppliers that have not confirmed.
done.remindersOff: Automatic reminders are off: the buyer reminds by hand.

stepUp.title: Confirm it’s you
stepUp.sentence: Switching automatic reminders on mails your suppliers. Type a fresh 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
stepUp.cancelled: Not switched: the code was not given. The reminders stay as they were.

problem.wrong: That code is wrong or already used. Type the code your app shows now.
problem.locked: Too many wrong codes. Wait a few minutes and try again.
problem.unavailable: The code could not be checked now. Try again.

keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keys.openRule: Open the rule in Admin › Approvals, automation & AI
keys.saveDialog: Save the tolerance in its dialog
